videos.script: Twenty past ten on a Monday. The till in Natal loses its connection. {{offline}} It keeps selling. Every sale waits in the till's memory. At two in the afternoon the line comes back, and thirty-eight sales arrive at once. {{burst}} Now count sales per minute. Count them by when they arrived, and Natal sold nothing all morning. Then, at two o'clock, a rush that never happened. {{arrival}} Count them by when they happened, and the morning is right. But the count for half past ten was wrong until two. {{event}} Every sale has three times. When it happened. When Kafka stored it. And when your program got to it. {{clocks}} A stream processor that does not choose one will use the nearest. The nearest is almost always the wrong one. {{choose}} In this lesson you send that Monday into Kafka. You measure how late the sales are, and how far out of order. And you count the same sales by both clocks, and see two different days. {{lab}}
